report.title: 2025 Annual Water Quality Report - CA4310011 San Jose Water Main System / CA4310018 City of Cupertino

sources_described: San Jose Water delivers a blend of local groundwater (88 wells; the report's 'Groundwater' column), surface water from SJW-managed watersheds in the Santa Cruz Mountains (Los Gatos Creek and Saratoga Creek, ~6,000 acres; 9 surface sources, treated by SJW; the 'Mountain Surface Water' column), and imported treated surface water purchased from Valley Water (the 'VW Surface Water' column; the map legend calls it 'Primarily SCVWD Imported Surface Water', and the p.6 footnote says these concentrations are provided by SJW's wholesaler). The p.5 map shows which source primarily serves each neighborhood.

extraction_notes: No violations or exceedances are disclosed: the president's letter states the results 'meet all state and federal drinking water standards' and every table row is marked 'Yes' under 'Met Drinking Water Standards?'. The document is a combined report for CA4310011 (San Jose Water Main System) and CA4310018 (City of Cupertino); its tables are not split by PWSID. Source columns: 'Mountain Surface Water', 'Groundwater', 'VW Surface Water' (Valley Water imported treated water). Cells printed N/A (Cryptosporidium and Giardia under Groundwater; Fluoride (treated) under Mountain Surface Water and Groundwater, footnote 2 'fluoride was not added') and NS = Not Sampled (Boron MSW+GW; Vanadium MSW; PFHxS/PFOA/PFOS under VW Surface Water) have no entry; the sibling entries' notes say so. pdftotext fuses footnote superscripts onto adjacent text on p.6 ('Turbidity1', 'N/A2', '0.753', '0.6-0.93'); the PDF content stream was inspected and the treated-fluoride values are 0.75 and 0.6-0.9 each carrying footnote 3; recorded as such. The Surface Water Treatment turbidity row prints a maximum under the Groundwater column (0.5 NTU, 100% <= 0.3 NTU) although footnote 1 says the TT applies only to surface water treatment; copied as printed. TTHM: printed Highest Site Average 47.7 ppb exceeds the printed Range of Results high 44.34 ppb; copied as printed. Lead: table 90th percentiles are 2.1 ppb (Spring 2025) and 1.6 ppb (Fall 2025) while p.12 text says the 2025 lead 90th percentile 'was below the lead detection limit'; table values used. Fall 2025 lead range high is 810 ppb (single sample, 1 of 102 > AL). Lead/Copper 'MCL' column prints action levels (AL=15, AL = 1.3). PFAS: the p.7 Notification Levels rows and the p.11 'Source Water PFAS Results' rows carry identical values; p.11 entries are included with notes beginning 'Duplicate:' so they can be de-duplicated; asterisked groundwater ranges include offline/standby wells that do not serve customers. Vanadium groundwater: average 21 ppb printed with range 'NS'. UCMR 5 rows (Lithium, PFHxS, PFOS) give only a Range of Results with no source column or average; value set to the range high. Secondary table's standard column is SMCL (recorded in mcl_printed); Notification Levels rows have no MCL (NL/RL recorded in notes). Where an average is printed ND but the range shows a detection, value is the range high (value_basis 'range_high'). Hardness appears twice (ppm and grains/gal), both kept. Specific Conductance unit printed 'µmho/cm'. Per-row sample years are not printed; sample_year 2025 reflects the report's data year except Cryptosporidium MSW ('2019 data'); the report warns 'Some of our data, though representative, are more than a year old.' Pages 1-5, 9-10 and 12-16 contain no further numeric data tables.
